title: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing
summary: Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing is a children's novel by Judy Blume, published by E. P. Dutton in 1972 with pictures by Roy Doty, and the first of her five Fudge books. Nine-year-old Peter Hatcher tells what life is like in a New York City apartment with his two-and-a-half-year-old brother, Fudge, whom everyone forgives no matter what he does. Fudge stops eating, knocks out his front teeth falling from a jungle gym, ruins Peter's school project and wrecks his own birthday party. Peter feels overlooked, and when Fudge is picked for a TV commercial he feels like a nothing. Then Fudge swallows Peter's pet turtle, Dribble. Underneath, the book is about brothers, being noticed and growing up, told with a lot of humor, and it ends with a gentle surprise: a puppy for Peter. Publishers Weekly said it would bring a chorus of laughter from sympathetic readers, and it won the Great Stone Face Award.

pieces.name: Central Park, New York City

pieces.about: Central Park is an urban park between the Upper West Side and Upper East Side neighborhoods of Manhattan in New York City that was the first landscaped park in the United States. It is the sixth-largest park in the city, containing 843 acres (341 ha), and the most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 42 million visitors annually as of 2016. It is also one of the most filmed locations in the world.

pieces.name: Boston
pieces.sentence: Mrs. Hatcher flies to Boston to visit her sister Linda, who has a new baby, leaving Mr. Hatcher alone with the boys for a weekend.
pieces.about: Boston, officially the City of Boston, is the capital and most populous city in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts in the United States. The city serves as the cultural and financial center of the New England region of the Northeastern United States. It has an area of 48.4 sq mi (125 km2) and a population of 675,647 as of the 2020 census, making it the third-largest city in the Northeast after New York City and Philadelphia. The Greater Boston metropolitan statistical area, including and surrounding the city, is the largest in New England and eleventh-largest in the country.

pieces.about: A doctor, also known as a physician, is a medical professional who is trained to diagnose and treat illnesses, injuries, and other health conditions. Doctors play a crucial role in maintaining public health, providing care and advice to patients, and advancing medical knowledge through research. Doctors are vital to the healthcare system, dedicated to diagnosing, treating, and preventing illnesses to improve patient health and well-being. The path to becoming a doctor is rigorous, requiring extensive education and training, but the profession is highly rewarding, offering the opportunity to make a significant impact on people's lives. As medical science and technology continue to evolve, the role of doctors will also adapt, ensuring that they remain at the forefront of providing high-quality healthcare.

pieces.name: Family Dynamics
pieces.sentence: Peter's parents give most of their time and attention to his toddler brother, Fudge, whose antics wreck a business dinner, a school project and a birthday party. Peter's family still loves him, and by the end they notice how he has coped. A reader sees how a busy family can overlook one child and how the love is still there.

pieces.name: Self Worth
pieces.sentence: When Fudge is picked for a TV commercial, Peter feels like a 'fourth grade nothing.' By the end his parents recognize how maturely he has handled things and give him a puppy of his own. A reader sees that feeling overlooked is not the same as not mattering.

pieces.name: Loss
pieces.sentence: Fudge swallows Peter's pet turtle, and although doctors help the turtle pass, Dribble has died. Peter is given a puppy and names him Turtle in memory. A reader sees that grief for a pet is real and that remembering can be a way to carry on.

pieces.name: Anger Management
pieces.sentence: Peter is easygoing until Fudge makes trouble; when his mother blames him after Fudge knocks out his teeth, he storms off and skips dinner, and she apologizes the next morning. A reader sees how a nine-year-old handles hot feelings and how a family can make up.

pieces.name: Parental Relationship
pieces.sentence: Peter's parents favor Fudge and sometimes blame Peter for what Fudge does, which hurts. His mother apologizes the next morning and his parents finally see how well he has coped. A reader sees that parents make mistakes and can put them right.
